# kamishibai

> kamishibai turns a list of words into an illustrated Anki deck — one card per word with a native example sentence, native-speaker audio, and a manga-style panel — using Google Gemini. It runs as an interactive terminal UI or as an asynchronous, session-based console flow built for agents.

This file documents the **console (session) flow**. Running `kamishibai` with no arguments opens the interactive TUI instead, which is out of scope here.

A session is a persistent, curatable unit of work an agent drives across separate invocations. It moves through stages:

1. **understood** — `new` understands each `--word` (or imports a cards JSON) and creates the session. The session now holds curatable candidates: per word, the senses the model proposed.
2. **(curate)** — optional: `select` which senses become cards, `exclude` a word, or `correct` a word to add senses. Each keeps the session understood.
3. **generating** — `generate` commits the curated plan and starts a managed background worker that produces the artifacts and publishes.
4. **published** — `result` returns the finished cards; `regenerate`/`fix` re-roll committed cards.

Generation is slow (Gemini per artifact, and the first publish parses system fonts for the PDF — expect tens of seconds). Poll `status` at a relaxed interval; do not tight-loop. Re-running is idempotent and cache-backed, so a killed `generate` resumes and only fills in what is missing. The interactive TUI (`kamishibai` with no arguments, or `kamishibai open <id>`) shares this same session model, so `ls`/`status` see interactive runs too.

## Output contract

The output is **plain text only — never JSON.** Everything is built so an agent needs only the `kamishibai` binary (no `jq`/`grep`/`sed`):

- **stdout carries the one capturable value**, bare: `new`/`select`/`exclude`/`correct`/`generate` print the session id (but `generate --wait` prints the three deck/pdf/dir paths instead, like `result`); `result --deck|--pdf|--dir` print one path. So `id=$(kamishibai new --word bank)` captures exactly the id.
- **stderr carries everything else**: the understood-senses preview, progress, hints, errors.
- `status`/`result`/`ls` print line-oriented text to stdout; `-q`/`--quiet` reduces each to its capturable essence (`status -q` → the phase word, `result -q` → the three paths, `ls -q` → ids).
- Exit codes are the script signal: `0` ok · `2` usage · `3` no such session · `4` not ready yet · `1` other error.

## Requirements

- `GEMINI_API_KEY` must be set; it is required for every flow that calls Gemini and wins over any saved key.
- The first OCR-backed run downloads PP-OCRv5 model files into the cache.

## Commands

- `kamishibai new --word WORD [--word WORD …] [--to LANG] [--from LANG] [--senses primary|all] [--build FILE] [--out DIR] [--id NAME] [--generate] [-q]` — understand each `--word` (repeat the flag, one card per word) and create a session in the **understood** stage. `--words FILE` or `--words -` reads words from a file/stdin instead. `--build FILE` imports a strict cards JSON path (or `-` for stdin) and skips understanding. `--senses` sets the initial sense selection (`primary` = the top sense; `all` = every sense); `select` overrides it later. `--generate` commits and starts the worker at once. Prints the understood senses to stderr and the bare session id to stdout.
- `kamishibai select <id> --card TERM --sense 1,3` — choose which 1-based senses of a card become cards (and re-include it). Resets the session to understood.
- `kamishibai exclude <id> --card TERM` — drop a card from the plan while keeping it visible in the understanding. Resets to understood.
- `kamishibai correct <id> --card TERM --note "..."` — ask Gemini to add senses to a card from an instruction. Resets to understood.
- `kamishibai generate <id> [--wait] [-q]` — commit the curated plan (deriving it from the selected senses) and start a managed background worker that generates the missing artifacts then publishes; prints the id and returns at once. `--wait` runs it in the foreground, streaming progress. Fails if nothing is selected.
- `kamishibai status <id> [-q]` — before a plan is committed: the curatable candidates with their senses and selection; after: per-card artifact progress. Read from the cache (no Gemini). `-q` prints only the phase word (`understood`/`generating`/`published`/`failed`/`interrupted`/`cancelled`).
- `kamishibai open <id>` — open the session in the interactive TUI, resuming from the cache.
- `kamishibai result <id> [--deck | --pdf | --dir] [-q]` — the finished cards (term, meaning, both example sentences, pronunciation, hint) plus the deck/pdf/dir paths. A selector (`--deck`/`--pdf`/`--dir`) prints exactly one path and takes precedence over `-q`; bare `-q` prints the three paths. Exits `4` if not published yet.
- `kamishibai regenerate <id> [--failed | --card TERM]` — drop cached artifacts so the next `generate` rebuilds them.
- `kamishibai fix <id> --card TERM --note "..."` — re-roll one committed card from an instruction (a Gemini call) and reset its artifacts.
- `kamishibai cancel <id>` — stop the running worker (leaves a published session published).
- `kamishibai ls [-q]` — list sessions (id · pair · phase · ready/total); `-q` prints only ids.
- `kamishibai rm <id> [--cache]` — delete the session, and with `--cache` its cached card folders.
- `kamishibai cache-path` — print the cache directory.

Supported language codes: `en`, `zh`, `es`, `ja`, `fr`, `de`, `ru`, `it`, `pt`, `el`.

## Example renderings

`kamishibai new --word "you're gonna get yours" --word bank --from ru --to en` (preview on **stderr**, id on **stdout**):

```
understanding 2 word(s) · ru → en
you're gonna get yours
  card  разг.   Идиом. «ты получишь по заслугам», обещание неизбежного наказания за проступки.
bank
  card  фин.    Сущ. «банк», организация для хранения денег.
  skip          Сущ. «берег» реки, озера, любого природного водоёма.
session en-…_0cfy · senses=primary · generate: kamishibai generate en-…_0cfy
```
```
en-…_0cfy
```

`kamishibai status <id>` while **understood** (stdout) — the curatable candidates, `*` marks a selected sense:

```
session  en-…_0cfy
pair     ru → en
senses   primary
phase    understood
words    2 understood · 2 card(s) selected
word  you're gonna get yours   card
  *  1  разг.   Идиом. «ты получишь по заслугам», обещание неизбежного наказания за проступки.
word  bank   card
  *  1  фин.    Сущ. «банк», организация для хранения денег.
     2          Сущ. «берег» реки, озера, любого природного водоёма.
out   /Users/you/kamishibai-out
```

Curate, then commit — e.g. keep only the river-bank sense of `bank`, then start generating:

```
kamishibai select en-…_0cfy --card bank --sense 2   # stderr: selected sense(s) 2 of 'bank'
kamishibai generate en-…_0cfy
```

`kamishibai status <id>` while **generating** (stdout) — `meta:ok scene:--` means present/absent; `status -q` prints just `generating`:

```
session  en-…_0cfy
pair     ru → en
senses   primary
phase    generating
worker   pid 48213 alive
cards    2 total · 1 ready · 0 failed
card  you're gonna get yours   meta:ok sound:ok scene:ok picture:ok   ready
card  bank                     meta:ok sound:ok scene:-- picture:--   building
out   /Users/you/kamishibai-out
```

`kamishibai result <id>` (stdout) — the finished cards plus paths:

```
session  en-…_0cfy
pair     ru → en
deck     /Users/you/kamishibai-out/en_….apkg
pdf      /Users/you/kamishibai-out/en_….pdf
dir      /Users/you/kamishibai-out

card 1/2  you're gonna get yours   importance 4
  meaning  ты получишь по заслугам, тебе это ещё аукнется
  say      jʊr ˈɡʌnə ˈɡɛt jʊrz
  en       Keep acting like a bully, and you're gonna get yours sooner or later.
  ru       Продолжай вести себя как задира, и «ты получишь по заслугам» рано или поздно.
  hint     Не официальный судебный вердикт punish, а зловещее обещание уличной мести.
```

`generate --wait` streams progress on stderr with stable tokens, then prints the three paths on stdout:

```
generating 2 card(s)…
  cache  you're gonna get yours · meta
  ok     bank · meta
  retry  bank · picture (1/3)
  ok     bank · picture
building deck and report…
done: 2 card(s) published
```

## Capturing values (no filtering)

```
id=$(kamishibai new --word "you're gonna get yours" --word bank --from ru --to en)
kamishibai exclude "$id" --card bank          # optional curation, prints "$id" again
kamishibai generate "$id"
while :; do
  case "$(kamishibai status "$id" -q)" in
    published) break ;;
    failed|interrupted|cancelled) echo "generation did not finish" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *) sleep 5 ;;
  esac
done
deck=$(kamishibai result "$id" --deck)
```

`status -q` can return any of `understood`/`generating`/`published`/`failed`/`interrupted`/`cancelled`, so a poll loop must break on every terminal phase, not just `published`, or it spins forever on a failed run.

## Cache

The cache directory is printed by `kamishibai cache-path` (macOS `~/Library/Caches/kamishibai`; Linux `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/kamishibai` or `~/.cache/kamishibai`; override with `KAMISHIBAI_CACHE`).

```
<cache>/cards/<from>-<to>/<key>/      meta.json  scene.json  voice.wav  illustration.jpg
<cache>/understanding/<from>-<to>/<key>.json
<cache>/sessions/<id>/                session.json  worker.log
<cache>/ocr-models/                   shared OCR model files
```

`<key>` is a short content hash. `status` derives each card's readiness by checking which artifact files exist; deleting a card's folder forces it to regenerate on the next `generate`. `session.json` additionally holds the typed words, the curated candidates, and the committed plan.

## Input

For `new` each word is one `--word` flag (one card per word); `--words FILE` reads one word per line and `--words -` reads stdin.

For `new --build FILE` the input is a strict cards JSON path (or `-` for stdin). Every field is required and unknown fields are rejected:

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "term": "lantern",
      "meaning": "a portable lamp",
      "pronunciation": "LAN-tern",
      "transcription": "/lantern/",
      "importance": 7,
      "source": {
        "sentence": "I carried a lantern through the dark hallway.",
        "lang": "en",
        "highlight": "lantern",
        "hint": "portable light",
        "context": "a simple everyday sentence"
      },
      "target": { "sentence": "Ich trug eine Laterne durch den dunklen Flur.", "lang": "de" }
    }
  ]
}
```

`importance` is an integer 1–10; text fields and language codes must be non-empty.
